page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 153 at upper right. Main text in one column on the left, with a narrow margin column to its right holding faint marginal notes. Below the text: a floral ornament, then the catchword-like word "SECT." at the foot, with a signature-like mark at the bottom left. main_text.p: næ totius illud est ; Impium hoc par dogmatum veræ Chriſti humanitati vim pa‐làm inferre ; neq; vnquam poſſe ſaluâ fide,cum ve‐ritate Euangelica conciliari.

page.notes: Faint marginal notes in the right margin (around the middle and lower part) are too faint and blurred to read reliably; they are not transcribed. Show-through from the reverse page is present across the text block and was ignored. The lower-left line "in" is partly visible and uncertain. The floral woodcut ornament sits between the text and the foot and carries no text. The word at the foot ("SECT.") is printed as a catchword-style mark; it is recorded as catchword. Long s was normalised to plain s in the text.
